title: Expected Unresolved-List Bound
summary: The cross-check analysis conjectures an inverse-success-probability bound on the expected maximum unresolved-list count, but a general proof or refutation remains open.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of candidate-list cross-checking in a pointwise-keyed weak-PRF key-recovery attack.
parameters: L: the unresolved candidate-list collection whose size governs cross-check cost
Pr[failure]: the failure probability appearing in the conjectured upper bound
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute the conjectured upper bound on the expected maximum number of unresolved lists.

citations.label: General Key Recovery Attack on Pointwise-Keyed Functions -- Application to Alternating Moduli Weak PRFs

progress.summary: The paper calls estimating the unresolved-list count from the failure probability nontrivial and explicitly conjectures the displayed bound. It provides parameter-specific Monte Carlo evidence but no general proof or refutation.
citation_labels: Antoine Sidem et al., General Key Recovery Attack on Pointwise-Keyed Functions -- Application to Alternating Moduli Weak PRFs
